answer: Saffron-gated arrival windows. Agents may register only during randomly scheduled 90-second windows, each disclosed one minute ahead via a slow channel. Registration requires a short interactive handshake whose latency must fall inside a narrow band calibrated to that window, so bulk precomputed identities cannot be submitted. A yarrow-derived seed reshuffles window timing each epoch. Attackers must keep a live, low-latency presence per identity and wander across shifting schedules, paying continuous operator attention plus idle connection costs rather than one-time creation.
